subject: switch on constructed number vs. functions

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: switch on constructed number vs. functions
parts:
I wanted to call out a design issue that's come up in the
command-line interface. This is all repeated on:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/392

If you'd prefer to read with GitHub formatting.

The code in question is this from gm/command.hpp:

...

} else if (algo->value() == "hmc") {

int engine_index = 0;
list_argument* engine = dynamic_cast<list_argument*>(algo->arg("hmc")->arg("engine"));
if (engine->value() == "static") {
engine_index = 0;
} else if (engine->value() == "nuts") {
engine_index = 1;
}

int metric_index = 0;
list_argument* metric = dynamic_cast<list_argument*>(algo->arg("hmc")->arg("metric"));
if (metric->value() == "unit_e") {
metric_index = 0;
} else if (metric->value() == "diag_e") {
metric_index = 1;
} else if (metric->value() == "dense_e") {
metric_index = 2;
}

int sampler_select = engine_index + 10 * metric_index + 100 * static_cast<int>(adapt_engaged);
switch (sampler_select) {
case 0: {
typedef stan::mcmc::unit_e_static_hmc<Model, rng_t> sampler;
sampler_ptr = new sampler(model, base_rng, &std::cout, &std::cout);
if (!init_static_hmc<sampler>(sampler_ptr, algo)) return 0;
break;
}
case 1: {
typedef stan::mcmc::unit_e_nuts<Model, rng_t> sampler;
sampler_ptr = new sampler(model, base_rng, &std::cout, &std::cout);
if (!init_nuts<sampler>(sampler_ptr, algo)) return 0;
break;
}
...

I have a very strong preference for more direct tests, that is,
not going through construction of an integer and then a switch.
This would replace all the above code with:

} else if (algo->value() == "hmc") {
list_argument* metric = dynamic_cast<list_argument*>(algo->arg("hmc")->arg("metric"));
std::string metric_config = metric->value();

list_argument* engine = dynamic_cast<list_argument*>(algo->arg("hmc")->arg("engine"));
std::string engine_config = engine->value();

if (metric_config == "unit_e" && engine_config == "static" && !adapt_engaged) {
typedef stan::mcmc::unit_e_static_hmc<Model, rng_t> sampler;
sampler_ptr = new sampler(model, base_rng, &std::cout, &std::cout);
if (!init_static_hmc<sampler>(sampler_ptr, algo)) return 0;
} else if (metric_config == "unit_e" && engine_config == "nuts" && !adapt_engaged) {
typedef stan::mcmc::unit_e_nuts<Model, rng_t> sampler;
sampler_ptr = new sampler(model, base_rng, &std::cout, &std::cout);
if (!init_nuts<sampler>(sampler_ptr, algo)) return 0;
}

I have a very strong preference for option 2. But an even
better version was suggested by Daniel as option 3:

std::string get_engine(const list_argument* algo) {
return algo->arg("hmc")->arg("engine")->value();
}

std::string get_metric(const algorithm& algo) {
... as above ...
}


std::string get_adapt_engaged(const list_argument* algo) {
... as above ...
}

bool is_unit_e_static(const algoright& algo) {
return "unit_e" == get_metric(algo)
&& "static" == get_engine(algo)
&& "engaged" == get_adapt_engaged(algo);
}

you need one of these for each algorithm, and then the switch becomes
even more readable:

if (is_unit_e_static(algo)) {
typedef stan::mcmc::unit_e_static_hmc<Model, rng_t> sampler;
sampler_ptr = new sampler(model, base_rng, &std::cout, &std::cout);
if (!init_static_hmc<sampler>(sampler_ptr, algo)) return 0;
} else if (is_unit_e_nuts(algo)) {
...

The general rule is to favor named functions for everything. Then

**test each of these functions with a simple unit test**.

The problem with option 1 above is that there's absolutely no way to
test the components of the embedded switch except from a top-level
command test.

Benefit number 2 is that it's much easier for the next person to read
the intent of the code and maintain it.

I'll do this for this code when I get a chance. I just made this

- Bob

I completely agree with Bob. When I was deep into the command stuff, the layout seemed reasonable, but now that I take a look again, it's hard to approach the code with fresh eyes because of the layout.

I created a second issue, #405, not realizing there was #390 open, but #405 is a little broader. It includes checking return codes. Other errors are masked due to command.hpp's structure.



Daniel
